analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 790-806): a new paragraph describing PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge, which caches token IDs for prompt pieces and renders Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS templates through ChatTemplateLoopRewrites. No source code or controls are modified in the supplied evidence, so there is no direct regression. The text claims reuse is scoped to the prefix-cache scope and never crosses scopes, can be disabled with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0, and that sampled background comparisons disable reuse on a mismatch. The implementing code (PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify those claims. Items for the next pass: (1) confirm the cache key includes the authenticated cacheScope (A-001, T-041), because an unscoped piece cache would add a cross-tenant timing oracle beyond the accepted SEC-035 risk; (2) confirm the in-memory token-ID cache holds plaintext-derived data only in process memory (T-011/T-014 class) and is bounded and cleared on unload; (3) check that the linear-time template rewrites are byte-equivalent to the reference template, since a mismatch would change the rendered prompt and tool/system boundaries; (4) check that parallel encoding on up to four cores does not exhaust resources. T-041 may warrant a threat-model note about the new prompt-token cache and its TTFT effect, which would sit alongside the prefix-cache TTFT oracle. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
